title: Predictable varying-particle SMC and reusable pilot stress

scope.theory: Bootstrap/Feynman-Kac particle filter where each generation's particle count/configuration is chosen from the completed past before the generation is sampled, propagation is conditionally independent given resampled parents, and resampling has the conditional unbiased empirical-measure property.
scope.resampling: Independent stratified resampling with arbitrary requested offspring count n and parent weights; no systematic-resampling variance claim.
scope.engineering: Synthetic two-state, 12-generation Feynman-Kac model with one discrete shock, total cost 768 particle-steps, 2,500 independent repetitions per shock position, fresh fixed seed 202608281905.
not_claimed: No universal MSE dominance of adaptive particle allocation.
No theorem for a configuration chosen using current-generation randomness before that generation's increment is formed.

public_evidence.source: Dau and Chopin, Waste-Free Sequential Monte Carlo, JRSS B 2022
public_evidence.use: Proposition 2 states that the product-of-average-potential normalising-constant estimate is unbiased in the SMC construction; the paper identifies this as the standard Del Moral unbiasedness result.

public_evidence.source: Douc, Cappe, Moulines, Comparison of Resampling Schemes for Particle Filtering, 2005
public_evidence.use: Section 2.3 defines independent stratified uniforms and states that for all integrable f the scheme satisfies the target weighted empirical expectation property; Section 3.3 gives lower conditional variance than multinomial. The construction allows offspring count n distinct from parent count m.

public_evidence.source: Zhou, Johansen, Aston, Toward Automatic Model Comparison: An Adaptive Sequential Monte Carlo Approach, 2016
public_evidence.use: Explicit warning that the standard normalising-constant estimate need not remain unbiased under generic adaptive SMC. This is why the derived lemma is restricted to predictable choices that do not alter the current target/increment using current-generation data.

derived_lemma.name: predictable-varying-N bootstrap-PF unbiasedness
derived_lemma.statement: Let F_{t-1} contain the completed particle system through t-1. Choose finite N_t>=1 and any generation-t tuning parameters F_{t-1}-measurably. Suppose resampling satisfies E[(1/N_t) sum_i f(X_{t-1}^{A_i}) | F_{t-1}] = sum_j W_{t-1}^j f(X_{t-1}^j) for every integrable f, and propagate each child through the fixed generation-t Markov kernel. Then the usual unnormalised particle measure is unbiased by induction; in particular E[Zhat_t]=Z_t.
proof_sketch: Condition on F_{t-1}; predictable N_t is then a constant.
The conditional unbiased-resampling identity converts the empirical parent average to the weighted parent measure, independently of whether N_t equals the previous population size.
Conditional expectation over propagation and the generation-t potential applies the Feynman-Kac operator Q_t.
Multiplying by the already accumulated normalising estimate and taking total expectation gives E[gammahat_t(f)]=gamma_t(f); set f=1 for Z_t.
derived_lemma.boundary: The induction does not cover choosing N_t or target/proposal parameters after inspecting generation-t particles in a way that changes the same increment, unless a separate proper-weight argument is supplied.

pilot_reuse_lemma.statement: If a completed pilot filter returns unbiased Zhat_p and its output chooses a fresh production configuration c, while E[Zhat_q | pilot]=Z for every c that may be selected, then any prespecified convex combination a Zhat_p +(1-a) Zhat_q is unbiased. The pilot-production covariance term is zero because E[Zhat_q-Z | pilot]=0.
pilot_reuse_lemma.safe_weighting: Use prespecified/cost-fixed blend weights. A pilot-dependent blend weight correlated with Zhat_p needs a separate proof.

designs.full_uniform: N_t=64 for all 12 generations; total cost 768.
designs.pilot: N_t=16 for all 12; cost 192; diagnostic is generation-local raw-potential CV^2.
designs.adaptive_production: remaining 576 particles allocated with q_t=(1-beta)/12 + beta*sqrt(0.05+CV2_t)/sum sqrt(...), beta=0.65, minimum 8.
designs.discard: adaptive-production Zhat only, thereby discarding pilot estimator despite paying its cost.

fresh_validation.interpretation: Reusing the pilot recovers most of the severe discarded-pilot cost penalty, but the naive local-CV2 allocator is not a robust improvement over a full uniform filter: average MSE is about 2.8% higher in this fresh stress and the worst discrete shock is about 17% higher. The strong t=0 gain (~22%) shows localization can help when the high-variance step is exactly where local CV2 is informative.

negative_result: Generation-local weight CV^2 is too myopic as the sole pilot diagnostic. It correctly places a large production allocation on the shock generation, yet later shocks often fail to beat uniform allocation. Particle-filter variance depends on ancestry and future continuation, so the next diagnostic must be Feynman-Kac/continuation-aware rather than purely local.
frontier: For the exact two-state model, compute generation-wise future-continuation functions and either an exact/asymptotic variance contribution or a brute-force oracle MSE gradient; use the pilot to estimate that quantity and rerun the reusable 192/576 design.
Formalise the predictable-varying-N induction in role state with all sigma-fields and verify the independent-stratified identity for n != m against the primary resampling construction.

Search whether an exact finite-sample adaptive-SMC theorem already covers predictable particle counts/configs; do not confuse it with generic adaptive tempering, for which standard Z estimates may be biased.
